title: Practice 4: при- and у-: arriving, and leaving

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Tom doesn't seem to be leaving.
exercises.why: **уходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **уходить** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **уйти**. present: я ухожу́ · ты ухо́дишь · он ухо́дит · мы ухо́дим · вы ухо́дите · они ухо́дят. — Wiktionary, «уходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приходит** (**приходить**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: We bring it from Switzerland.
exercises.why: **привозим** is the present tense (1st person plural) of **привозить** (to bring, to fetch by vehicle) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **привезти**. present: я привожу́ · ты приво́зишь · он приво́зит · мы приво́зим · вы приво́зите · они приво́зят. — Wiktionary, «привозить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «привозить — привезти — to bring (by vehicle).» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **увозим** (**увозить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Practice makes perfect.
exercises.why: **приходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **приходить** (to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **прийти**. present: я прихожу́ · ты прихо́дишь · он прихо́дит · мы прихо́дим · вы прихо́дите · они прихо́дят. — Wiktionary, «приходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда? — Это старшина. Лейтенант в штабе? — Нет, он уже идёт (едет) сюда.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **уходит** (**уходить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **ушли** is the past tense (plural) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **пришли** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. The other choice: **улетел** (**улететь**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
